name: isaac_like
display_name: ISAAC-CE (32 nm analog ReRAM, Shafiee 2016, simulated): 16128 arrays of 128 x 128

named: one ADC on the fused accumulator (per-array ADC not built, W47)
faithfulness.note: A design-space study, not a fabricated chip: every energy constant multiplies a published power by the paper's 100 ns cycle (isaac_like.json validity, shafiee2016isaac Table I).

notes: allow_coalescing and allow_neuron_splitting are true: "Since the operation requires a logical crossbar array of size 256 x 256, it must be spread across 4 physical crossbar arrays of size 128 x 128", whose ADC results "are then fed to the shift-and-add units, where the results are merged with the output register (OR) in the IMA", and "may undergo another step of shift-and-adds and merging with the central OR in the tile if the convolution is spread across multiple IMAs" (shafiee2016isaac, Section V, the Figure 4 example): a dot product's rows (partial sums) and its output columns span several arrays. onchip_arithmetic declares the lane subset L, E and P (on by default for value-domain chips, owner 2026-10-15; the off ablation declares classes [] through target_overrides with a note): ReLU as the law's clamp, a fused add and a requantizing average pool run on chip when the program is on the integer path (readout_law); a float value program keeps its host ops. The lane block is ng45_os_lane (an output-stage lane synthesized at 45 nm and 1.1 V, arith_toggle.md section 6, estimated; the resolver scales its area by node^2 and its energy by node x V^2 to this target's node, naming the factor in each row), one lane per 64 output columns, so 2 lanes per core (128 output columns per array). The certified function applies one ADC to each column's fused accumulator, while the cost model prices one conversion per array: the two are identical where adc_bits reaches an array's accumulator width, and below it the checked accuracy is not the priced chip's (per-array ADC, W47, not built). The bundle binds activation_bits 16: "Instead of a single voltage level that represents a 16-bit fixed-point number, we provide 16 voltage levels sequentially, where voltage level i is a 0/1 binary input representing bit i of the 16-bit input number." (shafiee2016isaac, Section V 'Input Voltages and DACs', PDF p.5); a run at another width declares it through target_overrides with a note.
